STATUS. This is a design only. No model was run. I changed no project file. I called no AWS and no outside model. I ran no project code. I read the files named here and ran small counting and arithmetic scripts in my temp folder.

THE QUESTION. Model B is Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, frozen. It answers a multiple-choice question about a short passage. Is it right more often when its prompt also holds a checked role description of that passage? A role description says which words occupy which Noetic ^1 to ^9, for which Mind, relative to what. It comes from the two label teams, and only where both teams agree.

WHAT DECIDES. 'Better' means better than the strongest ordinary help of the same length. Ordinary help is plain notes from an equally strong model that never saw the CAS guide. Beating 'no notes' is not enough.

SECOND QUESTION, SAME RUN. Do the role notes break answers B already gets right?

THIRD QUESTION, SAME RUN. NEW IN THIS VERSION. Do the role names add anything beyond pointing at the right words? A role note also points B at the sentences that matter. So the run must include a note that points at the same words with no role name. The one pass code now needs the role notes to beat that note too.

WHAT THIS IS NOT. This is the owner's option B. It tests whether the information is useful. It does not test any reader. The owner's sentence stands: "A later test must still show that the internal reader can supply equally useful descriptions."

FOUR OBJECTIONS IT IS BUILT TO ANSWER. 'It was just more words.' 'A strong model summarised the passage.' 'The answer leaked.' 'It only pointed at the right sentence.' Each has its own control group or check below.

THE SIZE TO EXPECT. The 428 labeled passages can give at most 300 final role-step tasks. How many survive the checks is NOT MEASURED. The most likely result is 100 to 140. By the fixed rule, a run with fewer than 200 final role-step tasks is exploratory, and every outcome code then ends in _EXPLORATORY. The real count is printed by the free build, before any money is spent, and the owner is asked the size question then.

CLAIM STATES USED HERE. REAL: counted by me today from the sealed files; the three reviewers got the same counts. PROPOSED: this design. EXPECTED: an estimate, not measured. ASSUMED: an input to a simulation, not a measurement. NOT MEASURED: nobody knows yet; the build or the practice phase will print it.

spec.task_design:
WHAT A TASK IS. One passage, one question, lettered options, exactly one right option. B replies with one JSON object, for example {"answer": "C"}. The right answer is one capital letter, as a string. Scoring is exact match on that letter.

FAMILY R: ROLE-STEP QUESTIONS (the benefit set). Every question adds a new condition that is not in the passage and asks what most likely follows. To answer, the solver must first know which thing plays which part, then take one more step. The question never asks 'which role is this?'.

SIX TYPES, TWELVE FORMS. A program opens a form for a passage only when the two teams agree on the entries it needs. No person chooses. Passage counts are REAL.
- BRING. Needs an agreed ^8 and an agreed ^9. 36 passages. Form 'Meet it again': later and elsewhere, which option would most likely bring the same thing back to the person? Form 'Take it away': suppose the noticed thing had not been there; which option would most likely not have happened?
- PULL-PUSH. 54 passages. Form 'Goes for' needs an agreed ^2: at a later free moment, which does the person choose? Form 'Keeps away' needs an agreed ^3: which does the person avoid?
- LAND. Needs an agreed ^4. 43 passages. Forms 'What stuck' and 'What slid off': at a later moment, which thing is the person most, or least, likely to bring up? A second LAND question is allowed only when the passage has two agreed ^4 entries.
- FORMED. Needs an agreed ^5. 45 passages. Form 'Swap the person': someone without that past stands in the same spot; what most likely goes differently? Form 'Where it helps': in which new situation would this background help most?
- PARTS. Needs two or more agreed ^6 entries. 37 passages. Form 'What is left': some named parts are dealt with; which named part is still left? Form 'Does not belong': a spare kit holds one of each named part; which of these would not be in it?
- HABIT. Needs an agreed ^7. 33 passages. Form 'After a long break': the repeated thing stops for a year or two; which action has most likely faded? Form 'New starter': someone on their first day takes the person's place; which of these would most likely be missing?
Together the types cover 192 passages. 137 open one type, 54 open two, 1 opens three.

FAMILY F: PLAIN-FACT QUESTIONS (the no-harm set). One per passage. A fact stated outright: where a thing was, who did what, which object. It must not depend on anyone's thoughts, likes, memories, habits or past, or on what a thing is made of. Four options. B gets the same notes as for that passage's role-step questions. A passage keeps its plain-fact task even if none of its role-step questions survive.

HOW MANY PER PASSAGE. At most two role-step questions. They must come from two different forms. Their right options must not be the same thing: the program compares the two right options with the looser word test in tools/verdict.py (half of the shorter text) and keeps only one if they match. Different types are preferred where the passage opens two.

CEILING (REAL, my recount; replaces the draft's 312 and 68). Under these rules the 156 final passages can carry at most 300 role-step tasks. 12 of them open only one form. The 34 practice passages can carry at most 66. With only one question per type, as the draft's wording implied, the ceilings would be 203 and 42.

OPTIONS. Each role-step question is written once, with one right option and five wrong ones in a fixed order.
- All six options are within 2 words of each other in length. No option is longer than 12 words.
- Every wrong option is a thing or an action named in the passage, or one that plainly fits it. No throwaway options.
- Where the form allows, the first wrong option uses the right option's things in a different relationship, for example the disliked thing where the liked thing is right. So 'pick the option whose words appear in the notes' does not find the answer.

DIFFICULTY DIAL. Level 1 shows four options: the right one and the first three wrong ones in the writer's order. Level 2 shows all six. The practice phase picks the level by a fixed rule. Plain-fact questions always show their four options. Nothing is rewritten after practice.

WORDS THAT MAY NOT APPEAR IN A QUESTION. The role notes speak in the canon lines. The ordinary notes are briefed in plain phrases. A question that shares the special words of either side would favor that side for a reason that has nothing to do with roles. So the question brief uses a third set of plain words, and the question sentence may not hold: the special words of the canon lines; the Noetic names; or the relation phrases of the ordinary-notes brief and of the plain-words frames (thoughts, drawn, put off, landed, lived, learned, pieces, made of, over and over, schedule). The full list is in Step 2.

WHY THE ROLE IS A NEEDED STEP. The new condition names one thing. The answer depends on the part that thing plays. BRING needs the direction of the pair. PULL-PUSH needs which thing the Mind is attracted toward and which it is repelled by. LAND needs the degree, kept apart from like and dislike. PARTS needs which named things the whole is composed of. HABIT needs what the repeated exposure conditioned. FORMED needs what the Mind is composed of.

WHY THE NOTES ARE NOT THE ANSWER KEY.
1. Notes are built per passage by a program from labels sealed on 2026-10-05. No question existed then.
2. Question writers never see any notes. Note writers never see any question.
3. Every question adds a condition that is in no note.
4. Up to two role-step questions per passage with different right things. One note text serves both.
5. Option letters are set by a seeded shuffle after everything else is frozen.
6. MIXED shows the same words with wrong role tags. QUOTES-ONLY shows the same words with no tags. Both are required groups.

WHAT STAYS TRUE AND MUST BE SAID. Every kept question turns on words the role note names. That is by rule (the anchor check). So the role note points at the right place and the ordinary notes do not. A reviewer counted this (REAL): of the 156 final role notes, 69 quote exactly one passage sentence and 44 hold exactly one entry besides ^1. MIXED carries the same pointing, so it cannot tell pointing from role names. QUOTES-ONLY can. That is why it is now in the pass rule.

LEFT OUT ON PURPOSE. No 'which statement matches the passage' level: it would be a copy of the note. No 'really there, or only in thought' type: the canon line for ^8 does not say the thing is physically present. No counting form for parts: where one team named a part the other did not, the count in the note would be wrong.

THE TWO OPEN DEFINITION QUESTIONS. No question may ask what a familiar sign means. No question may ask about a conclusion someone worked out. The 104 passages touched by rule 15 are not used at all.

HONEST LIMIT. A correct role note does make a role question easier. That is the thing being measured. The ordinary notes get the same chance, from an equally strong model that is told in plain words what kinds of question will come.

NOT MEASURED. Nobody has run B on questions like these. My guess is 40% to 60% right at four options. Only the practice phase can tell.

The examples in example_tasks use made-up passages. They are never cases.
example_tasks:
EXAMPLE 1 (made-up passage, never a case). Type BRING, form 'Meet it again'. Roles ^8 and ^9.

PASSAGE: Halima unlocked the boathouse and the smell of wet rope met her at the door. At once she was thinking of her uncle's ferry, the bench by the engine hatch, the tin of biscuits he kept under it. She hung the key on its nail and began counting the oars.

QUESTION: On another day, far from the boathouse, which of these would most likely make Halima picture her uncle's ferry again?
Writer's fixed order: right option 'smelling damp rope on a quay'; wrong 1 'hanging a key on a nail'; wrong 2 'counting a row of wooden oars'; wrong 3 'unlocking a heavy wooden side door'; wrong 4 'opening a door early in the morning'; wrong 5 'putting a key back in a pocket'. All six are 6 or 7 words. The right option is not the longest.
Anchors given by the writer: 'the smell of wet rope'; 'her uncle's ferry'.
Level 1 as B sees it after the seeded shuffle:
A. hanging a key on a nail
B. counting a row of wooden oars
C. smelling damp rope on a quay
D. unlocking a heavy wooden side door
RIGHT ANSWER: {"answer": "C"}
The question sentence holds none of the barred words (it says 'picture', not 'thoughts').

WHY THE ROLE IS A NEEDED STEP: the solver must know which thing did the bringing (the rope smell) and which was brought (the ferry). Then it must match 'damp rope on a quay' to the first. No note mentions a quay or another day.

GROUP ROLE (exact format the program writes; the first line is the padding line that every group carries):
Notes:
[Padding: neutral]
^1 Mind — Various degrees of awareness that processes, stores, outputs, and intakes Ideas.
^8 Above/Cause — An Idea that triggers a different Idea than itself to come to Mind.
^9 Below/Effect — The Idea brought to Mind by an Above/Cause trigger.
- ^1 Mind: "Halima".
- ^8 Above/Cause: "the smell of wet rope". For the Mind "Halima". Relative to "her uncle's ferry". Supporting quote: "Halima unlocked the boathouse and the smell of wet rope met her at the door."
- ^9 Below/Effect: "her uncle's ferry". For the Mind "Halima". Relative to "the smell of wet rope". Supporting quote: "At once she was thinking of her uncle's ferry, the bench by the engine hatch, the tin of biscuits he kept under it."

GROUP MIXED: the same text, but "the smell of wet rope" carries the ^9 Below/Effect tag and line, and "her uncle's ferry" carries the ^8 Above/Cause tag and line.

GROUP QUOTES-ONLY: the padding line (longer here, sitting where the canon lines sit in ROLE), then: - "Halima". - "the smell of wet rope". Supporting quote: "Halima unlocked the boathouse and the smell of wet rope met her at the door." - "her uncle's ferry". Supporting quote: "At once she was thinking of her uncle's ferry, the bench by the engine hatch, the tin of biscuits he kept under it." No Noetic, no Mind, no related thing, no definition line, no heading of its own.

GROUP ORD-INFORMED (an illustration written by me to show form; the real note is written by DeepSeek, which never sees a question, a label or the guide): the padding line, then: Halima opens the boathouse and smells wet rope. The smell at once makes her think of her uncle's ferry and small things on it: a bench by the engine hatch and a biscuit tin under it. The rope smell is at the boathouse now. The ferry is only a memory. Nothing says she likes or dislikes anything here. No habit or long training is described. Plain details: she hangs the key on its nail and starts counting the oars.

SECOND QUESTION ON THE SAME PASSAGE, DIFFERENT FORM AND DIFFERENT RIGHT THING (form 'Take it away'): Suppose the boathouse had not smelled of wet rope that morning. Going only by the passage, which of these would most likely not have happened? Right option 'Halima picturing the tin of biscuits'. Wrong options: 'Halima unlocking the old boathouse door'; 'Halima hanging the key on its nail'; 'Halima counting the oars one by one'; 'Halima walking in through the door'; 'Halima starting her usual morning jobs'. The same notes serve both questions, with two different right things.

EXAMPLE 2 (made-up passage, never a case). Type PULL-PUSH, form 'Goes for'. Roles ^2, ^3 and ^4.

PASSAGE: Odette walked the Saturday market with her list. The stall of old maps pulled her in; she turned the sheets slowly and forgot the time. The fish counter beside it made her wrinkle her nose and step wide around it. The brass band on the corner barely registered. She bought leeks and went home.

QUESTION: Odette has ten free minutes at the same market next week. Going only by the passage, where is she most likely to spend them?
Writer's fixed order: right option 'at the stall of old maps'; wrong 1, the swapped relationship, 'at the fish counter beside it'; wrong 2 'near the brass band on the corner'; wrong 3 'choosing leeks at a vegetable stall'; wrong 4 'reading her list by the gate'; wrong 5 'walking straight home with her bag'. All six are 6 or 7 words.
Level 1 as B sees it after the seeded shuffle:
A. at the fish counter beside it
B. near the brass band on the corner
C. at the stall of old maps
D. choosing leeks at a vegetable stall
RIGHT ANSWER: {"answer": "C"}
The notes name three of the four shown options, so matching words does not pick the answer. B must use which thing she is attracted toward.

GROUP ROLE:
Notes:
[Padding: neutral]
^1 Mind — Various degrees of awareness that processes, stores, outputs, and intakes Ideas.
^2 Positive — An Idea the Mind has an affinity for and is attracted toward.
^3 Negative — An Idea the Mind is adverse to and repelled by.
^4 Vibration — The degree to which an Idea resonates with the Mind, its impression.
- ^1 Mind: "Odette".
- ^2 Positive: "The stall of old maps". For the Mind "Odette". Supporting quote: "The stall of old maps pulled her in; she turned the sheets slowly and forgot the time."
- ^3 Negative: "The fish counter". For the Mind "Odette". Supporting quote: "The fish counter beside it made her wrinkle her nose and step wide around it."
- ^4 Vibration: "barely registered". For the Mind "Odette". Relative to "The brass band on the corner". Supporting quote: "The brass band on the corner barely registered."

GROUP MIXED (same words, wrong tags, by the fixed swap table): "The stall of old maps" carries ^3 Negative, "The fish counter" carries ^2 Positive, "barely registered" carries ^7 Rhythm. Each tag brings its own canon line. This version points at option A.

GROUP ROLE-PLAIN (only if the owner approves the frames; study wording, not a definition): Odette is drawn toward "The stall of old maps". Odette is put off by "The fish counter". How strongly or weakly "The brass band on the corner" landed with Odette: "barely registered". Then the same three supporting quotes.

GROUP ORD-INFORMED (illustration written by me): Odette is shopping at a Saturday market. She is drawn to a stall of old maps and loses track of time there. She is put off by the fish counter next to it and walks wide around it. She hardly notices the brass band on the corner. No memory is brought back and no long habit is described. Plain details: she has a list, she buys leeks, she goes home.
(Note how strong this rival is. A good plain note already says what she likes and dislikes.)

SECOND QUESTION ON THE SAME PASSAGE, DIFFERENT TYPE AND DIFFERENT RIGHT THING (type LAND, form 'What slid off'): That evening a friend asks Odette what she remembers of the market. Going only by the passage, which is she least likely to bring up? Right option 'the brass band on the corner'. Wrong options: 'the fish counter and its smell'; 'the stall of old maps'; 'losing track of the time'; 'the leeks she took home'; 'the list she carried round'. The trap is to mix up 'disliked' with 'hardly registered'.

EXAMPLE 3 (made-up passage, never a case). Type HABIT, form 'After a long break'. Role ^7.

PASSAGE: Every weekday for eleven years Oksana had weighed out flour at the same bench before dawn. Now her hands stopped the scoop at four hundred grams without a glance at the scale. A new radio played on the shelf. She tied her apron and called for the trays.

QUESTION: Oksana takes a desk job for two years and never weighs flour. Going only by the passage, which of these has most likely faded when she comes back?
Writer's fixed order: right option 'stopping the scoop without a glance'; wrong 1 'tying her apron at the bench'; wrong 2 'calling out for the trays'; wrong 3 'hearing the radio on the shelf'; wrong 4 'finding her bench before dawn'; wrong 5 'reading numbers on the scale'. All six are 5 or 6 words.
Anchors given by the writer (one or two are allowed): 'Every weekday for eleven years'; 'her hands stopped the scoop'. The first matches the agreed ^7 entry, so the question passes the anchor check. This is why two anchors are allowed: for ^7 and ^4 the agreed label is the pattern or the degree, not the thing the right option names.
Level 1 as B sees it after the seeded shuffle:
A. tying her apron at the bench
B. stopping the scoop without a glance
C. calling out for the trays
D. hearing the radio on the shelf
RIGHT ANSWER: {"answer": "B"}

GROUP ROLE:
Notes:
[Padding: neutral]
^1 Mind — Various degrees of awareness that processes, stores, outputs, and intakes Ideas.
^7 Rhythm — The rate and pattern a Mind is exposed to an Idea, entraining/conditioning it.
- ^1 Mind: "Oksana".
- ^7 Rhythm: "Every weekday for eleven years". For the Mind "Oksana". Relative to "weighed out flour". Supporting quote: "Every weekday for eleven years Oksana had weighed out flour at the same bench before dawn."
(If only one team had also given a ^5 entry on the scoop sentence, it is left out of the note and counted as 'only team A' or 'only team B'.)

GROUP ORD-INFORMED (illustration written by me): Oksana has weighed flour at this bench every weekday before dawn for eleven years. Her hands now know the amount: she stops the scoop at four hundred grams without checking the scale. Nothing is said about what she likes or dislikes. No memory is brought back. Plain details: a new radio plays on the shelf, she ties her apron, she calls for the trays.

WHY THE NOTE IS NOT THE KEY: the role note names the pattern and the activity. The faded skill is in no role note. B must carry the pattern to the break.

EXAMPLE 4 (short). Plain-fact question for the no-harm check, on the Example 3 passage. QUESTION: Where was the new radio? A. on the shelf. B. on the bench. C. beside the scale. D. in the tray rack. RIGHT ANSWER: {"answer": "A"}. No role is needed. Every group gets its usual notes for this passage. The check is whether a note makes B lose this easy answer. Note for the answer-leak screen: the ordinary note above says 'a new radio plays on the shelf'. Under the draft's screen that note would have been refused, because it holds the right option's text. Under the corrected screen it passes: 'on the shelf' is passage text, and the passage is in every prompt.
spec.how_questions_and_answer_keys_are_made_a:
Everything here happens before model B runs once. It costs no AWS money.

RULE ABOVE ALL. Nobody who has seen a label, a role note, the labeling guide or any other note writes or edits a question, a key or an ordinary note. The operator (Claude Code) can open every file, so it only runs programs. Every removal comes from a program rule and is logged with its reason. A custody file records who could open which file.

ORDER OF SEALS. Each is a hash written before the next step starts.
1. THE PLAN FIRST: pass rules, sizes, both briefs, the forbidden-word lists, the plain-words frames, the three closing wordings, the scorer version. With it: the label files, the 104-passage exclusion list, the eligible list with open forms, the 8 practice settings and the 4 reserve settings in order. (The draft sealed the plan last. A rule that is written after questions exist cannot be checked.)
2. Role notes (ROLE, MIXED, QUOTES-ONLY, and ROLE-PLAIN if approved).
3. Practice questions and keys. Then the practice set is fixed. Then final questions and keys.
4. Ordinary notes.
5. Assembled prompt parts and the removal log.
6. The programs: scorer, runner, gate program, analysis program. The reviewer checks them against the sealed plan.
Only then may B run.

STEP 1. QUESTION WRITER. Gemini gemini-2.5-flash, one passage per call, no memory between calls. It wrote the passages. It was never a label team and never saw the guide. Fallback: Codex/GPT by hand-off. Claude does not write questions, because Claude agents get the CAS definitions in their project instructions and cannot be blind.
- It writes for ALL 293 K1 to K5 passages, not only the eligible ones. So being asked tells it nothing. REAL: 58 of them are in the practice settings, 235 in the final settings.
- It sees one passage, the question brief and the format rules. It never sees the guide, the definitions, any label, any note or any other question.
- THE QUESTION BRIEF describes the twelve forms in its own plain words. They differ on purpose from the words of the ordinary-notes brief. They are study text, never definitions. Wording: BRING 'something a person notices makes them remember or picture something quite different'. PULL-PUSH 'the passage shows a person plainly liking one thing, or plainly keeping clear of one'. LAND 'the passage says something hit a person hard, or hardly at all'. FORMED 'a person's years of background change how they handle something now'. PARTS 'the passage lists the named parts of a thing'. HABIT 'doing the same thing again and again at set times has changed what a person does without trying'.
- For EACH FORM it judges the passage to support, it returns one question: the form name, the question, the right option, five wrong options in a fixed order (the swapped-relationship option first where the form has one), and one or two anchors. An anchor is an exact stretch of passage words, at most 8 words, that the question turns on. It also returns one plain-fact question with four options.
- All six options within 2 words of each other in length. No throwaway options.
- A second, separate writing pass with the same brief gives a spare question per form. A spare is used only where the first question for that form was dropped by a program check.
- Forbidden kinds: a question about what a sign means; a question about a conclusion someone worked out.

STEP 2. FORM CHECK BY PROGRAM. A role-step question is dropped if: it does not have exactly six different options; an option is longer than 12 words or the question longer than 45; the options differ by more than 2 words in length; one option sits inside another; it says 'all of the above' or 'none of the above'; an anchor is not an exact copy of passage words or is longer than 8 words; or it holds a forbidden word.
Forbidden in the question and in every option: the passage writer's own list in tools/write_verdict_passages.py line 19 (cause, effect, trigger, positive, negative, vibration, rhythm, idea, mind, noetic, resonate, resonance); the sign ^; the words Female, Male, Above, Below, CAS; the special words of the canon lines (affinity, attracted, adverse, repelled, impression, impregnated, composed, entraining, conditioning).
Forbidden in the question sentence only, NEW: the relation phrases of the ordinary-notes brief and of the ROLE-PLAIN frames (thoughts, drawn, put off, landed, lived, learned, pieces, made of, over and over, schedule). Options are built from passage things and may hold these everyday words.
Reason: no side's notes may share relation words with the questions. The outside reviewer reads the question brief and the ordinary-notes brief side by side before the seal.

STEP 3. TWO LABEL CHECKS BY PROGRAM. This is the only place labels touch questions. The writer never learns what was kept.
(a) ANCHOR CHECK. A role-step question is kept only if the passage is eligible, its form is open, and at least one of its anchors matches an agreed entry of the Noetic its form needs. 'Matches' is the looser test already in tools/verdict.py (the two texts share at least half the content words of the SHORTER one). The anchor is compared with either team's quote for that entry and, where the entry has a related thing, with either team's quote for the related thing. Reason for the looser test: a reviewer showed that with the strict test a writer who quotes a whole sentence would pass for only 19% to 78% of agreed entries, depending on the Noetic.
(b) OPTION CHECK, NEW. A role-step question is set aside when any of its six options matches, by the same looser test, an entry of the needed Noetic that only one team gave. For ^4 and ^7 the option is also compared with that entry's related thing. This removes questions where the role note is known to be short on the very point asked.
Both checks are counted and logged by reason.

STEP 4. KEY CHECK BY TWO BLIND SOLVERS FROM TWO FAMILIES. DeepSeek deepseek-chat in a fresh call, and a Claude Sonnet sub-agent given text only, with no file access. Each sees the passage, the question and the six options in shuffled order. Neither sees the writer's key, any note or any label. Each answers one letter, or 'more than one fits', or 'none fits'. A question is kept only if both pick the writer's right option and neither raises a flag.

STEP 5. NO-PASSAGE CHECK. The same two solvers, in separate calls, get the question and options with no passage. If both pick the right option, the question can be guessed from common sense and is dropped.

STEP 6. SELECTION BY PROGRAM. At most two role-step questions per passage, from two different forms, with right options that are not the same thing (looser test), different types preferred, chosen by seed. One plain-fact question per passage. Right letters are then set by a seeded shuffle so each letter is right equally often within each type and level. Backstop: across the kept set the right option may be the single longest or single shortest of its six options in at most 35% of tasks; seeded drops enforce it and are counted.

STEP 7. ORDINARY NOTES, THEN THE ANSWER-LEAK SCREEN. Ordinary notes are written only after the questions are sealed (see guidance_groups). Then one program screens every note of every group.
A note is hit if it holds any of these:
(a) an option letter written as a choice, such as 'A.', '(B)' or 'answer: C', outside text copied from the passage;
(b) the question sentence, word for word;
(c) the full text of an option that is NOT in the passage. An option that is passage text is not tested, because the passage is in every prompt;
(d) the whole word 'answer', 'option' or 'correct', counted only outside passage text. For a program-built note this means its fixed frame words only. For an ordinary note it means the note holds the word more often than the passage does. REAL: 4 eligible passages hold the whole word 'correct' in their own text (V027, V231, V335, V413).
WHAT A HIT DOES. A hit never causes any note to be written again. The passage is dropped for every group, by the program, with the reason logged. So the answer key can never decide what the rival may say.
The draft's screen refused any note that held an option's text. Options are built from passage things, so that screen would have hit most notes and had no stated consequence. This version replaces it.

STEP 8. ONE REVIEW ROUND. An outside reviewer (the DeepSeek reasoning model, as before) reads the plan, the code, all practice items and a seeded 10% sample of final items. It gets a checklist: the eight fixed rules listed in primary_comparison_and_pass_rules, the two briefs side by side, throwaway options, and the runner's file rules. Reviewers do not edit. The owner may read the practice items and a seeded sample of 20 role notes.

PRACTICE FIRST. The questions for the 8 practice settings are written and checked first. This costs no AWS money and spends no final passage. The program prints how many questions survive each filter: written by the writer for an open form; form check; anchor check; option check; key check; no-passage check; selection; length backstop.
RESERVE RULE. If fewer than 36 practice role-step tasks survive, reserve settings move from final to practice one at a time, in the sealed order (a cheese cellar, a boxing gym, a post office sorting room, a taxi rank at night), until 36 is reached. REAL: with 9, 10, 11, 12 practice settings the practice passages are 40, 45, 47, 50 and the final passages 150, 145, 143, 140. This is done before any final question is written. If 12 settings do not reach 36, do not launch; report the survival numbers to the owner. No brief and no filter is changed without a new reviewed plan version.

LAUNCH FLOOR. Do not launch with fewer than 100 final role-step tasks, fewer than 100 final plain-fact tasks, fewer than 36 practice role-step tasks or fewer than 20 practice plain-fact tasks.

OWNER CHECKPOINT. After the full build the owner gets the real counts and the detection table for those counts, and settles the size question then.

SURVIVAL IS NOT MEASURED. The draft said about 70%. That was a guess for several filters in a row. A reviewer's reading is that 100 to 140 final role-step tasks is most likely. The spare pass, the looser anchor test and the option-length rule are there to raise it. The option check lowers it.

HONEST LIMIT. A key that the writer and two language models agree on is a consistent key. It is not proof of a right key, most of all for 'most likely' questions.

guidance_groups.name: 1. NONE (no notes)
guidance_groups.what_model_b_gets: Passage, question, options, closing instruction. There is no Notes block at all.
guidance_groups.how_it_is_made: The fixed prompt frame with the Notes block removed.
guidance_groups.why_it_is_there: The baseline. Its accuracy is the difficulty number that must land in the window in practice. It also defines which tasks B 'already gets right' for the no-harm check.

guidance_groups.name: 2. FILLER (same length, no information)
guidance_groups.what_model_b_gets: A Notes block that holds the padding line and then the sentence 'No notes are provided for this passage.', to the same token count as the other notes for that passage.
guidance_groups.how_it_is_made: By the program. The padding line is '[Padding: neutral neutral ...]', sized with B's own tokenizer inside the job.
guidance_groups.why_it_is_there: Answers 'it was just more words'. It is the yardstick for how many right answers flip for no reason. It also feeds one fixed rule: if FILLER is 5 or more points below NONE and the test confirms it, padding itself hurts B and nothing is read from the run.

guidance_groups.name: 3. ROLE (checked role description; the one tested group)
guidance_groups.what_model_b_gets: The padding line. Then the canon definition line, word for word, for each Noetic that appears in the passage. Then one line per agreed entry: Noetic number and name, short label, for which Mind, relative to what, and the full supporting sentence. Example 1 shows the exact text.
guidance_groups.how_it_is_made: By the program from the two teams' agreed entries only. No person or model writes it. Entries only one team gave are left out and counted. Built and sealed before any question exists. No heading that claims authority.
guidance_groups.why_it_is_there: This is the owner's option B: 'carefully checked role descriptions from the labeling teams'. It is the only group the pass rule is about. The definition lines are printed because a small model would otherwise read Female, Male, Positive and Negative in their everyday sense. Whether the lines may be printed is an owner question.

guidance_groups.name: 4. MIXED (same words, wrong roles)
guidance_groups.what_model_b_gets: The ROLE text with every role tag swapped by one fixed table: ^2 with ^3, ^5 with ^6, ^8 with ^9, ^4 with ^7. ^1 stays. Each swapped tag brings its own canon line. Labels, Minds, related things and supporting sentences stay where they were.
guidance_groups.how_it_is_made: By the program, mechanically, from the ROLE text. The table follows the framework's own pairs (^2 with ^3, ^5 with ^6, ^8 with ^9) and swaps the two that are left.
guidance_groups.why_it_is_there: Required by the directive ('mixed-up CAS guidance'). If ROLE does not beat MIXED, the gain did not come from knowing which thing occupies which role. Limit: ROLE can also beat MIXED only because wrong tags mislead B. REAL: of the 54 PULL-PUSH passages, 28 have both ^2 and ^3 agreed, so the swap points at a named wrong option; 26 have only one, so the swap gives the right thing the opposite tag. That is why QUOTES-ONLY is now required as well.

guidance_groups.name: 5. ORD-INFORMED (ordinary notes, told the kinds of question; the strongest fair rival)
guidance_groups.what_model_b_gets: The padding line, then free plain-language notes on the passage, sized to match the ROLE text in tokens.
guidance_groups.how_it_is_made: DeepSeek deepseek-chat, one passage per call, temperature 0, no memory. It is the same model as label team B, so it is no weaker than the source of the role notes. Brief, with no CAS word: 'A weaker reader will be asked multiple-choice questions about this passage. You do not know the questions. They may ask what brought what into someone's thoughts, what someone is drawn toward or put off by, how strongly or weakly something landed, what a person has lived or learned, what named pieces a thing is made of, what someone does over and over on a schedule, and plain details. Write the notes that would help most. Plain words. Add nothing the passage does not support. About N words.' It never sees a question, an option, a key, a label, the guide or a role note. It writes three lengths per passage (see 'How length is matched'). Gemini then says pass or fail on 'every sentence is supported by the passage'. A failed note is written again once by the same blind process. This support check is the only thing that can cause a rewrite. The answer-leak screen never does.
guidance_groups.why_it_is_there: Answers 'a strong model summarised the passage'. The label teams were told by the guide what relations to look for. So the fair rival is told the same thing in plain words. I expect it to be hard to beat.

guidance_groups.name: 6. ORD-FREE (ordinary notes, told nothing about the questions; rival 2)
guidance_groups.what_model_b_gets: The padding line, then free plain-language notes, sized the same way.
guidance_groups.how_it_is_made: Same writer, same checker, same blindness, same length rule. The brief is the ORD-INFORMED brief without the sentence that lists the kinds of question.
guidance_groups.why_it_is_there: It is 'ordinary help' in the everyday sense. ROLE must beat BOTH rivals, which is the same as beating the stronger one, and nobody picks the rival after seeing results. The gap between the two rivals shows how much the plain hint is worth.

guidance_groups.name: 7. QUOTES-ONLY (the pointing without the roles; NOW REQUIRED)
guidance_groups.what_model_b_gets: The padding line, then the same labels and supporting sentences as ROLE. No Noetic, no Mind, no related thing, no definition line, no heading of its own. Role-step tasks only.
guidance_groups.how_it_is_made: By the program from the same agreed entries. Its padding line is long, because the canon lines and tags are gone. The padding sits at the start, exactly where the canon lines sit in ROLE.
guidance_groups.why_it_is_there: The role note points B at the sentences that matter. That may help by itself. QUOTES-ONLY sits between ROLE and MIXED: right tags, no tags, wrong tags. CHANGE: it is in the must-run block and in the time gate, and the one pass code needs ROLE to beat it. Without it, a pass could be earned with the role names doing no work.

guidance_groups.name: 8. ROLE-PLAIN (same role information, no CAS notation; secondary; ONLY if the owner approves)
guidance_groups.what_model_b_gets: The padding line, then the same entries, labels and supporting sentences as ROLE, written as plain sentences. No ^ numbers, no Noetic names, no definition lines, no ^1 line. Role-step tasks only.
guidance_groups.how_it_is_made: By the program, with seven fixed sentence frames that reuse the plain kind descriptions already frozen in 06_VERDICT_PLAN_v1_2.md: '<Mind> is drawn toward "X".' '<Mind> is put off by "X".' 'How strongly or weakly "Y" landed with <Mind>: "X".' 'What <Mind> has lived or learned: "X".' '"X" is one of the named pieces of "Y".' 'For <Mind>, "Y" came over and over on this schedule: "X".' 'For <Mind>: noticing "X" brought "Y" into their thoughts.' The frames are study control text. They are not definitions and not CAS. DEFAULT: the group is struck unless the owner approves or corrects the frames before the seal.
guidance_groups.why_it_is_there: It separates 'role information helps' from 'CAS notation helps'. Its result is printed only as a lead. It has no mixed-up control of its own, so it can never turn into a pass.

guidance_groups.name: Practice only: ANSWER-GIVEN
guidance_groups.what_model_b_gets: The padding line, then a note that states the right letter. Practice role-step tasks only. Never on a final task.
guidance_groups.how_it_is_made: By the program from the practice keys.
guidance_groups.why_it_is_there: Checks that B reads the Notes block at all. In the pilot B's answer never changed under the CAS text. CHANGE: the 90% bar is counted only among replies that are one allowed letter. Format is judged by its own gate.

guidance_groups.name: NO-PASSAGE (a task check, not a help group)
guidance_groups.what_model_b_gets: The question and options with no passage and no notes.
guidance_groups.how_it_is_made: By the program. Run on practice role-step tasks as a gate. Run on final role-step tasks last, reported only, and the first block to be dropped if time is short.
guidance_groups.why_it_is_there: Shows how much B can guess with no text. CHANGE: the practice gate stops only if B without the passage is above chance plus 15 points. The draft subtracted two noisy numbers; a reviewer showed that stopped a sound set 29% of the time.

guidance_groups.name: How length is matched (every group that has a Notes block)
guidance_groups.what_model_b_gets: For each passage, the same number of tokens in the Notes block in every group. Every group carries the padding line as the FIRST line of the block, ROLE and MIXED included. No group has padding next to the question.
guidance_groups.how_it_is_made: 1. The ordinary notes are sized by a count that includes punctuation: every word counts one and every punctuation mark counts one. Role notes are full of quote marks and signs, so matching by words alone would leave the ordinary notes 17% to 31% short in tokens (two reviewers' estimates). 2. The ordinary writer writes three lengths per passage: 90%, 100% and 110% of the ROLE note's count. Each must pass the support check. 3. Inside the job, with no model call, B's own tokenizer counts every block. For each passage and rival the program takes the length whose token count is nearest to the ROLE note's. This choice looks at length only. 4. The target for a passage is the largest block among its groups plus the shortest padding line. Every block is padded up to it at the start. One token of difference is allowed and recorded. 5. FIXED RULE, checked in the self-test before any model call: if the average padding is above 10% of the Notes block in ROLE, MIXED, ORD-INFORMED or ORD-FREE, the job stops with GATE_STOP_PADDING. No task is spent. Average padding per group is always reported.
guidance_groups.why_it_is_there: 'Same length' is checked by token count, not by eye. The draft matched words when writing and tokens when running, and put the padding at the tail. Then only the ordinary notes would have ended in padding right before the question, and ROLE could have won for that reason. The laptop does not run the tokenizer, which is why three lengths are written and the choice is made in the job. NONE is shorter by design; FILLER covers that.

leakage_and_fairness_controls: The plan is sealed first. Pass rules, briefs, forbidden lists, frames, closing wordings and the scorer version are hashed before any question is written. Labels were sealed on 2026-10-05. Role notes are hashed before any question is written. Questions and keys are hashed before ordinary notes are written. Everything is hashed before the job is built. The guest refuses a package that does not match the seal.

Who sees what. Question writer: one passage and the question brief. Key solvers: passage, question, options. Ordinary-note writer: one passage and its brief. Note checker: passage and the note, pass or fail only. None of them sees labels, role notes, keys or each other's work. All calls are stateless and logged with hashes.
Questions are written for all 293 K1 to K5 passages, so being asked carries no signal.

CORRECTED: tasks are kept by program rules that use the labels. The anchor check keeps a role-step question only when the words it turns on match an agreed entry. The option check sets a question aside when an option matches an entry only one team gave. So every kept question turns on something the role note names. This is a stated design choice, not blindness. No person picks tasks, and no rule looks at model B's answers. The pointing advantage this gives the role notes is measured by QUOTES-ONLY.
Same notes, different right answers. Notes are fixed per passage. Up to two role-step questions per passage must come from different forms and have different right things, checked by a word test.

Never the answer in the guidance: one screen for every group. It tests option-letter patterns, the question sentence, option text that is not in the passage, and the words 'answer', 'option', 'correct' outside passage text. A hit drops the passage for every group. A hit never causes a rewrite.

Shared words are treated the same on both sides. A question may not hold the special words of the canon lines, the Noetic names, or the relation phrases of the ordinary-notes brief and the ROLE-PLAIN frames. The question brief uses a third set of plain words. The outside reviewer reads the two briefs side by side.
No-passage screen before any B run: a question both outside solvers can answer without the passage is dropped.

Strength parity. The ordinary notes come from the same model as label team B, with the same passage, the same token budget and the same blindness to the questions. One rival is also told the kinds of question in plain words, as the label guide told the teams what to look for.
The role notes must beat each ordinary rival, not just the weaker one, and by at least 5 points over the better one.
The role notes must also beat QUOTES-ONLY for the one pass code. If they beat ordinary help but not QUOTES-ONLY, the code says so in its name.

Same frame for every group: the heading 'Notes:', the padding line first, then the content. No group has a heading that claims authority. Exact token-count equality of the Notes block per passage. Average padding above 10% in ROLE, MIXED or either ordinary group stops the job before any model call.
Same closing instruction, same decoding, same 64-token cap, same scorer for every group. The scorer is never told the group.

Format guard. If the share of replies that are not one allowed letter differs between ROLE and an ordinary group by more than 5 points, and the test confirms it, the outcome is FORMAT_GAP_NOT_READABLE. A difference in how B shapes its reply is then not read as a difference in understanding.
Right letters are balanced within each type by a seeded shuffle, so 'always answer A' scores exactly chance. Option order is identical across groups. B's letter counts are reported per group.

A word-matching rule with no model in it (pick the option that shares most content words with the notes) is scored for every group and printed beside B's scores. The ROLE-against-ordinary difference is printed again on the tasks where that rule does not pick the right option under ROLE.
For both ordinary groups the report prints the share of kept questions whose anchor words appear in that group's note.

Practice and final are split by whole settings before any final question is written: 8 practice settings, 4 reserve settings in a sealed order, the rest final. A practice task is never a final task. No final prompt is sent to the model until every practice gate has passed.

The two open definition questions are kept out. All 104 passages where either team wrote a rule-15 entry are unused, which includes all of K6 and K7. The question brief forbids sign-meaning and worked-out-conclusion questions.

Key custody in the job. Final keys sit in a separate folder. The stages that call model B are given the prompt folder only. The scoring stage opens the key folder after all outputs are written and hashed. Every prompt's full text is logged.
The passage, not the task, is the unit in every test, because two questions on one passage are not independent.

Nothing changes after the seal. Between practice and final only pre-written program choices apply: the closing wording, the option level, and which secondary blocks fit. After final outputs exist: no dropped case, no changed threshold, no new scoring rule.
The operator may not write or edit a question, key or note. This is custody by rule and by record, not by lock.
No harm is judged against FILLER only. The ordinary notes may simply help with facts; that is not the role notes doing harm.
ROLE-PLAIN and QUOTES-ONLY are derived from the role reading. They are never counted as ordinary help.
No Worlds, Domains, Drives or Registers appear in any text. Noetics are written ^1 to ^9. Definitions are quoted word for word and never reworded.
spec.practice_run_and_task_selection:
PURPOSE. Set the difficulty so that B alone is right 30% to 70% of the time, on practice tasks only. Prove the scorer, the prompt frame and the two result programs. Touch no final task with the model.

ONE JOB. Practice is phase 1 of the same job. Its gates are a program with fixed rules. The final phase starts only if every gate passes. The cost of this choice: no person reads B's raw practice answers before final tasks are used.

SPLIT (counts are REAL for this seed). random.Random(20261005).sample(sorted setting names, 12) gives 12 settings. The first 8 are the practice settings: a locksmith's van, a tailor's shop, a mountain hut, a quarry, a dairy at milking time, a chess club, a swimming pool, a beekeeper's yard. I checked that these are the same 8 the draft drew. The next 4 are the reserve, in this order: a cheese cellar, a boxing gym, a post office sorting room, a taxi rank at night. With 8 practice settings: 34 eligible practice passages (BRING 5, PULL-PUSH 11, LAND 8, FORMED 8, PARTS 7, HABIT 4) and, after removing V009 and V076, 156 final passages (BRING 30, PULL-PUSH 43, LAND 35, FORMED 37, PARTS 29, HABIT 29).

PRACTICE TASKS. At most 66 role-step and 34 plain-fact tasks (REAL ceiling). How many survive is NOT MEASURED. The floor is 36 and 20. The reserve rule in the question section applies if the floor is missed.

WHAT THE JOB DOES, IN ORDER.
Gate 0, self-test, no model loaded.
- The scorer gives the hand-decided category on every known example.
- Package hashes match the seal. Every task has every group. The GPU is present; the runner refuses a CPU with GPU_REQUIRED.
- The tokenizer loads. The padding plan and the hash of every practice and final prompt are computed and saved. No final prompt is sent to the model.
- PADDING RULE: average padding above 10% of the Notes block in ROLE, MIXED, ORD-INFORMED or ORD-FREE stops the job (GATE_STOP_PADDING).
- NEW: the gate program and the analysis program are run from start to end on five made-up answer sets built from the practice tasks. Each must print the code worked out by hand in the plan: every reply right gives UNINFORMATIVE_DIFFICULTY; every reply wrong gives UNINFORMATIVE_DIFFICULTY; a designed set (ROLE right on every role-step task, every other group right on every second one, plain facts all right) gives BEATS_ORDINARY_HELP_NO_HARM_NOT_MEASURED_EXPLORATORY; fixed-seed random letters must give a listed code that is not the pass code; every reply malformed gives INVALID_RUN. The seconds taken are recorded. The score stage's time limit is set to 5 times that, and at least 120 seconds. If 5 times the measured time is above 240 seconds, stop (GATE_STOP_SELFTEST).
- Then the guest marks setup complete, before the first model call (see the AWS section).
Gate 1, closing wording. Three closing instructions are fixed in the plan. B alone answers every practice task at level 1 under each. The wording with the most replies that are exactly one allowed capital letter is used. Ties go to the first listed.
Gate 2, difficulty. B alone on practice role-step tasks at level 1 (four options) and level 2 (six options). Window for level 1: 35% to 70%. Window for level 2: 30% to 70%. The lower edge is the larger of 30% and chance plus 10 points. If both levels are in their window, the one nearer 50% is taken; a tie goes to level 1. If one is, that one. If none, stop.
Gate 3, no-harm base. B alone must be right on at least 60% of practice plain-fact tasks. Else stop.
Gate 4, format, at the chosen level. In each of the seven must-run groups at least 75% of practice replies must be exactly one allowed capital letter, and FORMAT_FAIL plus CUT_OFF must be at most 25%. Else stop. CHANGE: a secondary group under the bar (ROLE-PLAIN, NO-PASSAGE) is dropped from the final phase. It does not stop the job.
Gate 5, notes are read. CHANGE: among ANSWER-GIVEN replies that are one allowed letter, at least 90% must be right. There must be at least 20 such replies. Else stop.
Gate 6, the passage is needed. CHANGE: stop only if B with no passage is above chance plus 15 points at the chosen level (above 40% with four options, above 31.7% with six). The difference from B alone is printed as a number.
Gate 7, time. From the measured seconds per call, the seven must-run groups on all final tasks must fit before the work cutoff (minute 135) with a 25% margin and 300 seconds to spare. Else stop. Secondary blocks are then added only if they fit, in this order: ROLE-PLAIN, NO-PASSAGE. This is decided once, before the first final call.

PRINTED BY THE GATE STEP, NO RULE ATTACHED. The share of practice role-step tasks on which ROLE and ORD-INFORMED give different results. The size table rests on an assumed value for this. The gap in clean replies between ROLE and each ordinary group.

STOP CODES. GATE_STOP_SELFTEST, GATE_STOP_PADDING, GATE_STOP_DIFFICULTY, GATE_STOP_NO_HARM_BASE, GATE_STOP_FORMAT, GATE_STOP_NOTES_NOT_READ, GATE_STOP_GUESSABLE, GATE_STOP_TIME.

CHANCE OF A STOP WHEN NOTHING IS WRONG (ASSUMED inputs; a reviewer's simulation, 20,000 runs; not rerun by me). In the central case (B alone 45% and 37%, no-passage 30%, plain facts 80%, 97% clean replies, notes read 95%) all gates pass 87% of the time with 50 practice tasks and 79% with 36. With the draft's rules it was 57% and 48%. So about 1 sound run in 5 to 8 still stops at a gate. A guessable set still gets through about 26% of the time, and unread notes 3% to 6%. The padding stop is not in these numbers.

AFTER A STOP. The final tasks were never sent to the model. They stay sealed and usable by a later reviewed job. Practice items may be used again as practice. They are never final tasks. Practice results are never reported as a finding about roles.

WHAT PRACTICE MAY NOT DO. It never picks or drops a single final task. It does not remove a question type: a type has only 4 to 11 practice passages, too few to judge it.

NOISE. With 36 to 50 practice role-step tasks, B's measured accuracy has a 95% range of about plus or minus 14 to 16 points. A final set that turns out too easy or too hard is caught again by the UNINFORMATIVE_DIFFICULTY rule. A reviewer's simulation puts that at 5% of runs or fewer after a go.

HONEST RISK. Nobody has run B on such questions. Both levels may fall outside the window. Then the job stops for under 1 USD and the final tasks stay unspent.
spec.sizes_and_what_can_be_concluded:
COUNTS (REAL, my arithmetic on the label files with the proposed seed).
- Eligible passages: 192. Practice 34. Final 156.
- Of the 156 final passages: 109 have at least one open type with no left-over entry on its needed Noetic. 49 have no left-over ^2 to ^9 entry at all. 137 open a type other than LAND or HABIT. 19 open only LAND or HABIT. 109 open one type, 47 open two.
- CEILING. Final role-step tasks: at most 300 (two per passage; 12 passages open only one form). Final plain-fact tasks: at most 156. Practice: at most 66 and 34. The draft's 312, 68 and 'about 215' did not follow from its own rules and are withdrawn.

HOW MANY WILL SURVIVE: NOT MEASURED. Six filters run in a row. My honest expectation, and a reviewer's: 100 to 140 final role-step tasks on 75 to 100 passages. The free build prints the real number per filter, on the practice settings first.

FIXED TIERS (unchanged).
- At least 200 final role-step tasks on at least 120 final passages: the outcome code is read as it stands.
- 100 to 199 tasks, or fewer than 120 passages: the same rule is applied and every outcome code ends in _EXPLORATORY. This is the tier to expect.
- Fewer than 100 tasks: do not launch.

ARITHMETIC FOR ONE COMPARISON. Every task is answered under every group, so groups are compared task by task. Suppose the role notes lift accuracy by 10 points over the best ordinary notes, and the two groups differ on 30% of tasks. For independent tasks:
n = (1.645 x sqrt(0.30) + 0.84 x sqrt(0.30 - 0.10^2))^2 / 0.10^2 = (0.901 + 0.452)^2 / 0.01 = 183 tasks
for an 80% chance of detection at the one-sided 5% level. That matches the directive's 'roughly 150 to 250'.

CHANCE OF THE ONE PASS CODE (my simulation today, 2,000 runs per cell, passage-level test, EVERY condition included: the five comparisons, the 5-point margin, beating QUOTES-ONLY, no-harm, the padding rule). ASSUMED, not measured: B alone 45%, filler 44%, ordinary free 52%, ordinary informed 56%, plain facts 80%; two questions on one passage move together. 'Gain' is the true gain of ROLE over the better ordinary notes.

CASE A, the kind case: MIXED 46%, QUOTES-ONLY 50%.
- 210 tasks on 140 passages. Groups differ on about 25% of tasks: gain 0 passes 3%; gain 5, 37%; gain 10, 77%; gain 15, 83%. Groups differ on about 40%: 2%; 19%; 59%; 79%.
- 130 tasks on 100 passages. 25%: 3%; 24%; 66%; 83%. 40%: 1%; 12%; 43%; 72%.
- 100 tasks on 75 passages. 25%: 2%; 19%; 53%; 76%. 40%: 1%; 9%; 30%; 60%.
The chance tops out near 82%. A harmless note still fails the no-harm check about 1 time in 10, and the padding rule trips about 1 time in 15.

spec.scoring:
THE YARDSTICK. The written rules C:/Users/wakil/OneDrive/Desktop/tksCAS/cas_only_reasoner/CASALESCENCE_NOETICS_v0_1/03_SCORER_RULES_v0_1.md and the source .../tools/scorer_v0_1.py, with one defect fixed. Five categories: CORRECT, WRONG, TYPE_MISMATCH, FORMAT_FAIL, CUT_OFF. Primary score: CORRECT = 1, everything else = 0. One code fence is read, as the rules say. All five counts are printed per group.

WHY LETTERS. The task answer is a one-letter string such as "C". A letter can be matched exactly. By the rules as written, "c", "C.", "(C)" and "C. the smell of damp rope" are WRONG. That is strict, and it is the same for every group.

THE DEFECT (REAL; I read the source again today). Rule 5 says the reply must be one object with exactly one key. The source reads the text with json.loads, which silently keeps the last of two repeated keys. So {"answer": "A", "answer": "B"} is read as "B" and accepted. A hedged double answer could be marked CORRECT.

WHICH VERSION RUNS (fixed now). Version 0.1.1: the same rules, and a repeated key is FORMAT_FAIL. The sealed plan names 0.1.1 and its hash. It is reviewed in the one review round with the plan. If the reviewer rejects the change, the plan is corrected to name 0.1 and sealed again before anything is built. The seal never names two versions.

ADDED KNOWN EXAMPLES (they change no rule). The 30 examples in .../scorer_examples_v0_1.json hold no single-letter case. Add about ten, decided by hand from the rules as written: "B" against "B" is CORRECT; "b" is WRONG; "B." is WRONG; "B. the side door" is WRONG; the number 2 is TYPE_MISMATCH; ["B"] is TYPE_MISMATCH; a fenced {"answer": "B"} is CORRECT; a fence on one line is FORMAT_FAIL; the repeated-key reply is FORMAT_FAIL.

WHAT THE RUNNER SUPPLIES. The cut_off flag: true when B wrote 64 new tokens with no end token.

TWO TERMS USED BY THE RULES.
- CLEAN REPLY: a reply scored CORRECT or WRONG whose value is one of the letters shown for that task.
- NOT CLEAN: everything else. That is FORMAT_FAIL, CUT_OFF, TYPE_MISMATCH and any WRONG reply whose value is not an allowed letter, such as "C. the smell of damp rope". The draft counted only FORMAT_FAIL and CUT_OFF. A dressed letter is scored WRONG, so it slipped past the format line.

FORMAT FLOOR. A group with more than 25% FORMAT_FAIL plus CUT_OFF on final tasks is at format floor and nothing is read from it. FIXED NOW: role-step tasks and plain-fact tasks are counted apart, and a must-run group must clear the line on both.

FORMAT GAP (new, see the pass rules). If the not-clean share differs too much between ROLE and an ordinary group, the outcome is FORMAT_GAP_NOT_READABLE.

THE RISK THAT LOOKS LIKE THE OLD FENCE PROBLEM. If B habitually writes "C. the smell of damp rope", every group scores zero. The rules stay strict. The guards are in practice: three closing wordings are tried and the cleanest is kept, and the final phase does not start unless at least 75% of replies in every must-run group are clean.

EXTRA VIEWS; NO PASS RULE MAY USE THEM. (1) Near-miss count: WRONG replies that are a valid letter with punctuation, or the exact option text. (2) Which letters B chose, per group. (3) The word-matching rule's score per group. (4) The NO-PASSAGE score. (5) Breakdown by question type. (6) The existing digit view from the rules.

WHERE SCORING RUNS. Inside the AWS job, as a separate stage, after all model calls are finished, their outputs hashed and the model files hashed again. The analysis program prints every number and the one outcome code. It uses whole-number counts and writes its result file so that a not-a-number value cannot appear. The report repeats the program's output. No status comes from prose. Anyone can repeat the scoring from the returned files.
spec.primary_comparison_and_pass_rules:
All of this is fixed before any question is written and is in the first seal. A program applies it and prints exactly one outcome code.

THE NUMBER COMPARED. For each group: the share of CORRECT answers over the final role-step tasks at the chosen level.

THE TEST FOR 'X BEATS Y'. For each final passage take d = (tasks CORRECT under X) minus (tasks CORRECT under Y). If the notes made no difference, each passage's d is as likely to be plus as minus. The program flips the signs at random 100,000 times (seed 20261005) and counts how often the flipped mean is at least as large as the real one. That share is p. 'Beats' means p is at most 0.05, one-sided. The measured difference and a 95% range (passages resampled 10,000 times, same seed) are always printed beside it. No correction for several tests is needed for the pass code, because every one of them must hold.

VALIDITY. If one fails the outcome is INVALID_RUN with the reason. No claim, no retry on these tasks, no dropped task, no changed threshold.
V1. Every planned final call in the seven must-run groups has an output.
V2. Model and tokenizer file hashes are the same at the start and after the last model call. The receipt of the second hash must exist; if it is missing the code is INVALID_RUN. The package matches the seal. Every prompt hash matches the dry build.
V3. None of the seven must-run groups is at format floor, on role-step tasks and on plain-fact tasks counted apart.

READABILITY. Checked next, in this order. If one fails, that code is the outcome and no gain or loss is read.
R1. UNINFORMATIVE_DIFFICULTY: B alone on the final role-step tasks is above 85% or below chance plus 5 points.
R2. FORMAT_GAP_NOT_READABLE: on final role-step tasks the not-clean share differs between ROLE and ORD-INFORMED, or between ROLE and ORD-FREE, by more than 5 points in either direction, AND the same passage-level test, two-sided, gives p at most 0.05.
R3. PADDING_HURTS_B_NOT_READABLE: FILLER is 5 or more points below NONE on final role-step tasks, AND the test 'NONE beats FILLER' holds.
Why R2 and R3 need the test as well as the 5 points: see the note at the end of this section.

CONDITIONS.
C1. ROLE beats NONE, and ROLE beats FILLER.
C2. ROLE beats ORD-INFORMED, and ROLE beats ORD-FREE, and ROLE's share is at least 5 points above the better of the two. If the two rivals tie, ORD-INFORMED is the better one.
C3. ROLE beats MIXED.
C4. The no-harm check is HELD (see no_harm_check).
C5. NEW: ROLE beats QUOTES-ONLY.

OUTCOME CODES, CHECKED IN THIS ORDER. These are study codes. They are not spec-sheet status words.
1. INVALID_RUN.
2. UNINFORMATIVE_DIFFICULTY.
3. FORMAT_GAP_NOT_READABLE.
4. PADDING_HURTS_B_NOT_READABLE.
5. NO_ROLE_HELP_SHOWN: C1 does not hold.
6. HELP_NOT_TIED_TO_CORRECT_ROLES: C1 holds, C3 does not.
7. ROLE_HELP_NOT_ABOVE_ORDINARY_HELP: C1 and C3 hold, C2 does not. Exact sentence for the report, CHANGED: 'Role information helped B. An advantage over a strong model's ordinary notes was not shown. A gain under about X points could have been missed.' The program computes X from the final data: the larger of (2.485 times the standard error of the ROLE-minus-better-rival difference) and (5 points plus 0.84 times that standard error), rounded up to a whole point. The draft's sentence said 'no more than', which claims a tie. This test cannot show a tie.
8. HELPS_BUT_BREAKS_RIGHT_ANSWERS: C1, C2, C3 hold, no-harm is NOT_HELD. Under the directive this is a failure of the stage. If no-harm is NOT_MEASURABLE the code is BEATS_ORDINARY_HELP_NO_HARM_NOT_MEASURED, which is not a pass.
9. POINTING_BEATS_ORDINARY_HELP_ROLE_NAMES_NOT_SHOWN, NEW: C1, C2, C3 and C4 hold, C5 does not. Exact sentence: 'The checked label-and-quote notes beat ordinary help. A gain from the role names beyond pointing at the words was not shown.' This is not the pass code. Whether it is reason enough to build the reader is an owner question.

spec.no_harm_check:
THE QUESTION. Do the role notes make B lose answers it gets right without them?

TWO MEASURES ON FINAL TASKS. BOTH MUST HOLD FOR 'HELD'.

H1. PLAIN-FACT TASKS. These need no role. B gets the same notes as for the role-step tasks of that passage. Loss = share right with no notes minus share right under ROLE. Rule: the measured loss is at most 5 points.

H2. KEEPING WHAT WAS RIGHT. Take every final task, both families, that B got CORRECT with no notes. Count the share still CORRECT under each group. Rule, CHANGED: the share kept under ROLE is not more than 5 points below the share kept under FILLER. FILLER is the only yardstick.
Why FILLER: some of B's right answers are lucky. Any change to the prompt flips some of them. FILLER changes the prompt and adds no information, so it shows how many flip for no reason.
Why the ordinary rival is no longer a yardstick here: the ordinary writer is told to include plain details. So its notes may keep more plain-fact answers just by repeating the fact. That is the rival helping, not the role notes harming. The draft had already dropped this comparison from H1 for that reason and kept it in H2 by mistake. The comparison with the better rival is still printed.

NOT MEASURABLE. Fewer than 100 final plain-fact tasks, or fewer than 80 final tasks CORRECT with no notes. Then the pass code is not available. The launch floor (100 final plain-fact tasks) and the practice gate (B alone at least 60% on practice plain-fact tasks) are there to prevent this.

ALWAYS PRINTED. The 95% range of each difference. The upper end of the one-sided 95% range of the H1 loss, inside the fixed sentence 'A loss of up to X points cannot be ruled out.' The same two measures for MIXED, QUOTES-ONLY and both ordinary rivals, so a reader can see whether a loss is special to the role notes or common to every note. The full two-by-two table against no notes for every group.

ARITHMETIC (my simulation today, 4,000 runs per line; ASSUMED: 125 to 135 plain-fact tasks, B alone right on 80%). With H1 and H2 together, the check is HELD 90% of the time when the true loss is 0; 47% to 52% when it is 5 points; 10% to 12% when it is 10 points; 1% when it is 15 points.

WHAT 'HELD' DOES AND DOES NOT MEAN. It rules out a large loss. It does not rule out a loss of 5 points (passes about half the time) or 10 points (passes about 1 time in 9). A harmless note fails about 1 time in 10. The rule uses the measured value and prints the range beside it. That is the convention the owner already accepted in 06_VERDICT_PLAN_v1_2.md.

NOT USED. K8 and K9 passages. Their role note says only that the teams marked nothing, so it is nearly filler. Adding them would water down the measured loss and make the check easier to pass.

NOT COVERED. What a 'nothing marked here' note does to B. That is left for a later test.

THE THREE CLOSING WORDINGS (fixed now; practice picks one; ties go to the first).
1. Return exactly one JSON object with key answer and no other text. The value of answer is one capital letter: A, B, C or D.
2. Reply with one JSON object only. Its single key is "answer". Its value is the capital letter of your choice (A, B, C or D) and nothing more. No option text, no explanation, no code fence.

2. run practice: the gated sub-steps.

spec.what_it_can_and_cannot_show:
IT CAN SHOW.
- Whether B answers role-step questions better with a role description both label teams agree on than with nothing, with filler, with wrong roles, with the same words and no role names, and with two kinds of ordinary notes of the same length from an equally strong model.
- Where a gain comes from: being pointed at key sentences (QUOTES-ONLY against the ordinary notes and FILLER), the role names on top of the pointing (ROLE against QUOTES-ONLY), wrong names (MIXED against QUOTES-ONLY), or the CAS notation (ROLE against ROLE-PLAIN, if that group is approved).
- Whether the role notes cost B a large share of answers it already had.
- If even agreed role descriptions do not help B, the internal reader is not worth building for this purpose with this model B and this prompt layout. That is the cheap early answer the owner asked for.

WHAT IT CAN CONCLUDE AT THE SIZE IT WILL MOST LIKELY REACH (100 to 140 final role-step tasks, labelled _EXPLORATORY).
- A large advantage, 15 points or more over the better ordinary notes, would usually be seen if the role names carry it.
- A 10-point advantage would be seen about 3 to 7 times in 10.
- A plain-fact loss of 15 points would be caught.
- It cannot reliably tell 'role names help' from 'pointing helps' unless the role names add about 12 points or more on top of pointing.
- A miss cannot tell 'no advantage' from 'an advantage under about 12 points'.
- HELD does not rule out a plain-fact loss of 5 points, and lets a 10-point loss through about 1 time in 9.

IT CANNOT SHOW.
- That a reader inside model A can supply such descriptions. The owner's words: "A later test must still show that the internal reader can supply equally useful descriptions." This job does not call model A.
- That the role descriptions are right. They are agreed between two language models. For 136 of the 192 usable passages they are also partial: some entry was left out because only one team gave it.
- That role notes help on questions in general. The role-step questions were chosen because they turn on roles, and every kept question turns on words the role note names. That is home ground for the role notes. A win means 'on questions that turn on these relations, where the checked description covers the point asked'. The informed ordinary rival and QUOTES-ONLY are there to make that ground as level as it can be. The plain-fact family only tests harm.
- That the help is special to CAS. Two ordinary rivals are not every rival. The directive's stricter test, a fair non-CAS set of roles labeled by the same independent process, is not in this job. No such claim may be made.
- Anything about sign reading or reasoned conclusions. Those 104 passages are left out until the owner rules.
- Anything about passages where the teams did not agree, or about questions that hinge on an entry only one team gave. Those are removed by rule.
- Anything firm about a single Noetic or question type. Those tables are small.
- Anything about ^4 Vibration and ^7 Rhythm beyond the passages where the teams happened to agree. The owner's point stands: their problem is presence, and this test does not repair it.
- Anything about ^0, about passages with no roles, about other model pairs, found text or longer passages. One 0.5B model, 53-word passages written by a language model to a brief, English, one prompt layout.
- Learning. Nothing is trained.

HOW EACH RESULT READS.
- ROLE_HELP_BEATS_STRONGEST_ORDINARY_HELP: the premise holds on this test, role names included. Building the reader gains a reason, pending replication on fresh passages.
- POINTING_BEATS_ORDINARY_HELP_ROLE_NAMES_NOT_SHOWN: checked label-and-quote notes beat ordinary help; the role names did not show an added effect. Whether that is enough reason to build the reader is the owner's call.
- ROLE_HELP_NOT_ABOVE_ORDINARY_HELP: an advantage over a strong model's plain notes was not shown; the report says how large a gain could have been missed.
- HELP_NOT_TIED_TO_CORRECT_ROLES: the notes helped, but right role names did no better than wrong ones.
- NO_ROLE_HELP_SHOWN or HELPS_BUT_BREAKS_RIGHT_ANSWERS: recorded as such, never softened.
- FORMAT_GAP_NOT_READABLE, PADDING_HURTS_B_NOT_READABLE, UNINFORMATIVE_DIFFICULTY, INVALID_RUN, or a gate stop: no finding about roles either way.

MY EXPECTATION, NOT A RESULT. The informed ordinary notes will be a hard rival. The most likely outcome is ROLE_HELP_NOT_ABOVE_ORDINARY_HELP or a miss, with the _EXPLORATORY ending. Either is a real answer, not a broken test.
